subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should compaction and memory flush be moved out of the foreground session lane, made preemptible within that lane, or kept serialized with a stricter timeout and user-visible busy/error path?
rationale: The remaining fix changes core scheduling and session-state semantics, and source inspection shows the issue is not just a missing timeout constant or narrow local bug.

options.title: Design isolated maintenance scheduling
options.body: Move or split compaction and memory flush onto a bounded maintenance path with explicit transcript/session ordering guarantees before implementation.

options.title: Keep serialization but improve recovery
options.body: Preserve the single-lane model and add stricter cancellation, timeout, and visible busy/error handling to reduce hangs without changing ownership boundaries as much.

options.title: Close after timeout mitigation only
options.body: Treat the 180-second timeout reduction as enough and leave longer architectural starvation cases to narrower future reports.

recommendation.title: Design isolated maintenance scheduling
recommendation.body: Move or split compaction and memory flush onto a bounded maintenance path with explicit transcript/session ordering guarantees before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest adjacent foreground-delivery deadlock fix sits closest to the scheduling and reply-path decision boundary this issue needs.
